claim: Ammonium serves as a key nitrogen source and metabolic intermediate.
source: Ammonium serves as key nitrogen source and metabolic intermediate, yet excess causes toxicity.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ammonium's biological role.

claim: Excess ammonium causes toxicity.
source: Ammonium serves as key nitrogen source and metabolic intermediate, yet excess causes toxicity.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ammonium toxicity.

claim: Ammonium uptake is mediated by ammonium transporters.
source: Ammonium uptake is mediated by ammonium transporters, whose regulation is poorly understood.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ammonium transport mechanisms.

claim: The regulation of ammonium transporters is poorly understood.
source: Ammonium uptake is mediated by ammonium transporters, whose regulation is poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Transport can easily be characterized in heterologous systems.
source: While transport can easily be characterized in heterologous systems, measuring transporter activity in vivo remains challenging.
evidence: This is established knowledge about experimental methods in the field.

claim: Measuring transporter activity in vivo remains challenging.
source: While transport can easily be characterized in heterologous systems, measuring transporter activity in vivo remains challenging.
evidence: This is a statement about current limitations in the field.

claim: A simple assay for monitoring ammonium transceptor activity in vivo was developed by inserting circularly-permutated GFP into conformation-sensitive positions.
source: Here we developed a simple assay for monitoring activity in vivo by inserting circularly-permutated GFP into conformation-sensitive positions of two plant and one yeast ammonium transceptors ('AmTrac' and 'MepTrac').
evidence: This is the primary finding of the manuscript, supported by experimental data throughout.

claim: Addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the sensors triggered concentration-dependent fluorescence intensity changes.
source: Addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the sensors triggered concentration-dependent fluorescence intensity (FI) changes that strictly correlated with the activity of the transporter.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in multiple figures including Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: The fluorescence intensity changes strictly correlated with the activity of the transporter.
source: Addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the sensors triggered concentration-dependent fluorescence intensity (FI) changes that strictly correlated with the activity of the transporter.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data including growth assays and fluorescence measurements shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Fluorescence-based activity sensors present a novel technology for monitoring the interaction of transporters with their substrates.
source: Fluorescence-based activity sensors present a novel technology for monitoring the interaction of the transporters with their substrates, the activity of transporters and their regulation in vivo
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: This technology is particularly valuable in the context of analytes for which no radiotracers exist.
source: which is particularly valuable in the context of analytes for which no radiotracers exist, as well as for cell-specific and subcellular transport processes that are otherwise difficult to track.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential applications of the technology based on its demonstrated capabilities.

claim: Transport proteins play critical roles in cellular uptake and release as well as subcellular distribution of ions and metabolites.
source: Transport proteins play critical roles in cellular uptake and release as well as subcellular distribution of ions and metabolites.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the function of transport proteins.

claim: Due to their hydrophobic nature, the characterization of transporters is challenging.
source: Due to their hydrophobic nature the characterization of transporters is challenging, and activity measurements typically depend on the use of radiotracers and heterologous expression systems.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the challenges in studying membrane proteins.

claim: Activity measurements of transporters typically depend on the use of radiotracers and heterologous expression systems.
source: Due to their hydrophobic nature the characterization of transporters is challenging, and activity measurements typically depend on the use of radiotracers and heterologous expression systems.
evidence: This is established knowledge about standard methods in the field.

claim: The development of electrophysiology tools was one of the major breakthroughs for characterizing channels.
source: One of the major breakthroughs for characterizing channels has been the development of electrophysiology tools, enabling characterization of electrogenic transport in live cells (Neher and Sakmann, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Neher and Sakmann, 1992.

claim: Electrophysiology tools enable characterization of electrogenic transport in live cells.
source: One of the major breakthroughs for characterizing channels has been the development of electrophysiology tools, enabling characterization of electrogenic transport in live cells (Neher and Sakmann, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Neher and Sakmann, 1992.

claim: Patch clamping has largely been limited to the analysis of processes at the cell membrane, or cells at the surface of sliced tissues.
source: However, patch clamping has largely been limited to the analysis of processes at the cell membrane, or cells at the surface of sliced tissues.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the limitations of patch clamp techniques.

claim: Fluorescent proteins enable observation of cellular processes in living cells of intact tissues.
source: A new level of insight was provided by fluorescent proteins enabling us to observe cellular processes in living cells of intact tissues (Tsien, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tsien, 2006.

claim: FRET sensors have allowed monitoring of analyte levels and dynamics in live cells with minimal invasive methods.
source: Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET) sensors have allowed us to monitor analyte levels and dynamics in live cells with minimal invasive methods (Okumoto et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Okumoto et al., 2012.

claim: Particular FRET sensors can be used to monitor biophysical processes such as membrane potential or tension between molecules in live cells.
source: Particular FRET sensors can even be used to monitor biophysical processes such as membrane potential or tension between molecules in live cells, as well as the conversion of substrates of enzyme reactions by proteases and kinases.
evidence: This is established knowledge about FRET sensor capabilities.

claim: It has not been possible to directly follow the activity of transporters and to monitor their regulation in vivo prior to this work.
source: Yet to date, we have not been able to directly follow the activity of transporters and to monitor their regulation in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field before this work.

claim: It may be possible to create transport activity sensors by monitoring structural rearrangements in a transporter with the help of environmentally sensitive genetically encoded fluorophores.
source: We rationalized that it may be possible to create transport activity sensors by monitoring structural rearrangements in a transporter with the help of environmentally sensitive genetically encoded fluorophores.
evidence: This is the hypothesis that motivated the experimental work.

claim: FRET can be used to probe conformational rearrangements based on the pioneering work of Miyawaki et al. (1997).
source: Based on the pioneering work of Miyawaki et al. (1997), FRET can be used to probe conformational rearrangements and has widely been exploited to develop genetically encoded sensors for small molecules.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Miyawaki et al., 1997.

claim: Circularly permutated GFP variants can be used as reporters for conformational rearrangements.
source: An alternative, again developed by Tsien's lab (Baird et al., 1999), is the use of circularly permutated GFP variants as reporters for conformational rearrangements
evidence: This is supported by citation to Baird et al., 1999.

claim: Circularly permutated GFP variants have been exploited to create sensors for small molecules such as calcium, zinc and maltose.
source: which have been exploited to create sensors for small molecules such as calcium, zinc and maltose (Baird et al., 1999; Marvin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baird et al., 1999 and Marvin et al., 2011.

claim: Circularly-permutated versions of GFP have successfully been used to monitor structural rearrangements of calmodulin.
source: Circularly-permutated versions of GFP (cpGFP) have successfully been used to monitor structural rearrangements of calmodulin (Baird et al., 1999; Nagai et al., 2001; Nakai et al., 2001; Wang et al., 2008; Akerboom et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: cpGFP is a protein in which the β-barrel structure has been rearranged in a way that ligand-induced conformational changes can influence the chromophore environment and consequentially the fluorescent properties of a chimeric sensor.
source: cpGFP is a protein in which the β-barrel structure has been rearranged in a way that ligand-induced conformational changes can influence the chromophore environment and consequentially the fluorescent properties of a chimeric sensor.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of cpGFP sensors.

claim: GFP and its variants have two excitation maxima (λex ∼ 395 and 475 nm) depending on pH.
source: Depending on pH, GFP and its variants have two excitation maxima (λex ∼ 395 and 475 nm) (Tsien, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tsien, 1998.

claim: Protein-cpGFP fusions, in which structural rearrangements affect the state of the chromophore as well as the hydrogen bonds between the chromophore and the surrounding β-barrel, can in principle be exploited to develop sensors that monitor transporter activity.
source: Protein-cpGFP fusions, in which structural rearrangements affect the state of the chromophore as well as the hydrogen bonds between the chromophore and the surrounding β-barrel, can in principle be exploited to develop sensors that monitor transporter activity.
evidence: This is the hypothesis being tested in the manuscript.

claim: The hypothesis tested was that ammonium transporters can effectively report transporter activity in live cells when fused to cpGFP.
source: Here we tested the hypothesis that ammonium transporters can effectively report transporter activity in live cells when fused to cpGFP.
evidence: This is the central hypothesis of the study.

claim: Ammonium transport is key to nitrogen nutrition of bacteria, fungi and plants.
source: Ammonium transport is key to nitrogen nutrition of bacteria, fungi and plants.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ammonium transport.

claim: Mammals are unable to assimilate ammonium into amino acids.
source: Although mammals are unable to assimilate ammonium into amino acids, ammonium transporters play key roles in renal ammonium secretion and male fertility (Biver et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mammalian metabolism.

claim: Ammonium transporters play key roles in renal ammonium secretion and male fertility in mammals.
source: Although mammals are unable to assimilate ammonium into amino acids, ammonium transporters play key roles in renal ammonium secretion and male fertility (Biver et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Biver et al., 2008.

claim: Transporters for ammonium are conserved in bacterial, fungal, plant and animal genomes.
source: Transporters for ammonium are conserved in bacterial, fungal, plant and animal genomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the evolutionary conservation of ammonium transporters.

claim: Ammonium transport is electrogenic.
source: Ammonium transport is electrogenic and is mediated by high affinity ammonium transporters of the AMT/MEP/Rhesus protein superfamily (Marini et al., 1994; Ninnemann et al., 1994; Tremblay and Hallenbeck, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Ammonium transport is mediated by high affinity ammonium transporters of the AMT/MEP/Rhesus protein superfamily.
source: Ammonium transport is electrogenic and is mediated by high affinity ammonium transporters of the AMT/MEP/Rhesus protein superfamily (Marini et al., 1994; Ninnemann et al., 1994; Tremblay and Hallenbeck, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The genome of Arabidopsis contains six AMT paralogs.
source: The genome of the plant Arabidopsis contains six AMT paralogs, four of which (AMT1;1, 1;2, 1;3, and 1;5) are partially redundant and together essential for ammonium acquisition (Yuan et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2007.

claim: Four AMT paralogs (AMT1;1, 1;2, 1;3, and 1;5) are partially redundant and together essential for ammonium acquisition in Arabidopsis.
source: The genome of the plant Arabidopsis contains six AMT paralogs, four of which (AMT1;1, 1;2, 1;3, and 1;5) are partially redundant and together essential for ammonium acquisition (Yuan et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2007.

claim: In plants, ammonium acquisition is highly regulated and is subject to feedback inhibition.
source: In plants, ammonium acquisition is highly regulated and is subject to feedback inhibition, potentially as a means of preventing accumulation of ammonium to toxic levels (Wang et al., 1993; Kronzucker et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wang et al., 1993 and Kronzucker et al., 2001.

claim: Feedback inhibition of ammonium acquisition potentially serves as a means of preventing accumulation of ammonium to toxic levels.
source: In plants, ammonium acquisition is highly regulated and is subject to feedback inhibition, potentially as a means of preventing accumulation of ammonium to toxic levels (Wang et al., 1993; Kronzucker et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations.

claim: Ammonium-triggered phosphorylation of a critical threonine in the cytosolic C-terminus of AMT1;1 leads to inhibition of ammonium transport by allosteric regulation in the trimeric transporter complex.
source: Recent results show that ammonium-triggered phosphorylation of a critical threonine in the cytosolic C-terminus of AMT1;1 leads to inhibition of ammonium transport by allosteric regulation in the trimeric transporter complex (Loqué et al., 2007; Lanquar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Loqué et al., 2007 and Lanquar et al., 2009.

claim: AMT1;3 functions as an electrogenic high-affinity ammonium transporter involved in nitrogen uptake in Arabidopsis roots.
source: The close homolog AMT1;3, also functions as an electrogenic high-affinity ammonium transporter involved in nitrogen uptake in Arabidopsis roots (Gazzarrini et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gazzarrini et al., 1999.

claim: AMT1;3 functions in homo- and hetero-trimeric complexes with the coexpressed AMT1;1 and is allosterically regulated.
source: AMT1;3 functions in homo- and hetero-trimeric complexes with the coexpressed AMT1;1 and is allosterically regulated (Yuan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2013.

claim: AMT1;3 not only functions as a transporter, but in addition controls root architecture by a process similar to the one found for the yeast MEP2 transceptor.
source: AMT1;3 not only functions as a transporter, but in addition controls root architecture by a process similar to the one found for the yeast MEP2 transceptor (dual function transporter and receptor), a protein that mediates ammonium transport and regulates pseudohyphal growth (Boeckstaens et al., 2007; Lima et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Boeckstaens et al., 2007 and Lima et al., 2010.

claim: MEP2 is a transceptor with dual function as transporter and receptor that mediates ammonium transport and regulates pseudohyphal growth.
source: AMT1;3 not only functions as a transporter, but in addition controls root architecture by a process similar to the one found for the yeast MEP2 transceptor (dual function transporter and receptor), a protein that mediates ammonium transport and regulates pseudohyphal growth (Boeckstaens et al., 2007; Lima et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Boeckstaens et al., 2007 and Lima et al., 2010.

claim: The term transceptor was introduced by Thevelein to describe the dual function of the general amino acid permease Gap1p or the phosphate transporter Pho84p in transport and signaling.
source: The term transceptor had been introduced by Thevelein to describe the dual function of the general amino acid permease Gap1p or the phosphate transporter Pho84p in transport and signaling (Kriel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kriel et al., 2011.

claim: Most of the progress in the ammonium transport field has been made with the help of yeast and Xenopus laevis oocytes as heterologous expression systems.
source: Most of the progress in the ammonium transport field has been made with the help of yeast and Xenopus laevis oocytes as heterologous expression systems.
evidence: This is a statement about the history and methods of the field.

claim: In planta studies mostly rely on the use of either stable isotopes (15N), or radiotracer analogs (14C-methylammonium).
source: By contrast, in planta studies mostly rely on the use of either stable isotopes (15N), or radiotracer analogs (14C-methylammonium).
evidence: This is a statement about current methods in plant research.

claim: Monitoring ammonium-induced depolarization of membrane potential has successfully been deployed in plants.
source: Monitoring ammonium-induced depolarization of membrane potential has successfully been deployed in plants (Wang et al., 1994), yet it can not differentiate between transport mediated by individual AMTs and non-selective cation channels.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 1994.

claim: Monitoring ammonium-induced depolarization of membrane potential cannot differentiate between transport mediated by individual AMTs and non-selective cation channels.
source: Monitoring ammonium-induced depolarization of membrane potential has successfully been deployed in plants (Wang et al., 1994), yet it can not differentiate between transport mediated by individual AMTs and non-selective cation channels.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the method.

claim: It has not been possible to identify the networks that regulate the substrate-triggered feedback inhibition of ammonium uptake in plant roots.
source: Therefore, it has not been possible to identify the networks that regulate the substrate-triggered feedback inhibition of ammonium uptake in plant roots.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations in the field prior to this work.

claim: There is a need for new tools that enable monitoring of transport activity in intact root tissues.
source: Thus there is a need for new tools that enable us to monitor transport activity in intact root tissues.
evidence: This is an inference about the needs of the field based on current limitations.

claim: An activity sensor was created by inserting cpGFP into a cytosolic loop of the Arabidopsis ammonium transporter AMT1;3.
source: Here we created an activity sensor by inserting cpGFP into a cytosolic loop of the Arabidopsis ammonium transporter AMT1;3.
evidence: This is the primary experimental finding of the manuscript.

claim: Thorough characterization demonstrates that the chimera reports processes that occur in the transport cycle.
source: Thorough characterization demonstrates that the chimera reports processes that occur in the transport cycle, although at present it is not possible to differentiate substrate binding or steps in the transport cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: At present it is not possible to differentiate substrate binding or steps in the transport cycle using the sensor.
source: Thorough characterization demonstrates that the chimera reports processes that occur in the transport cycle, although at present it is not possible to differentiate substrate binding or steps in the transport cycle.
evidence: This is a statement about the current limitations of the sensor.

claim: This approach is transferable to other proteins, supported by the successful creation of additional sensors for the Arabidopsis paralog AMT1;2 as well as the distantly related yeast ammonium transceptor MEP2.
source: We project that this approach is transferable to other proteins, a notion supported by the successful creation of additional sensors for the Arabidopsis paralog AMT1;2 as well as the distantly related yeast ammonium transceptor MEP2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing successful creation of AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac (Figure 9).

claim: AMT1;3 has eleven transmembrane helices organized in a pseudo-symmetric structure with an extra terminal TMH-XI that directs the C-terminus to the cytosol.
source: Eleven TMH are organized in a pseudo-symmetric structure (TMH I-V and TMH VI-X) with an extra terminal TMH-XI that directs the C-terminus to the cytosol.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A based on HMMTOP prediction.

claim: Fluorescent proteins were inserted into different cytosolic loops of AMT1;3 to test functionality.
source: Figure 1B shows the functionality of the transporters was measured as growth of the yeast Δmep1,2,3 mutant transformed with AMT1;3-FP fusions
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B with growth assays.

claim: AMT1;3 with mcpGFP inserted at position 233 in loop L5-6 retained transport functionality.
source: Figure 1B shows growth complementation assay results for different insertion positions
evidence: This is shown by growth on ammonium-containing media in Figure 1B.

claim: A three-dimensional model of AMT-mcpGFP chimeric protein was created based on crystal structures of Af-AMT1 and cpGFP.
source: Three-dimensional model of one AMT-mcpGFP chimeric protein based on the crystal structures of Af-AMT1 (2B2H) and cpGFP (3evp).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C and described in the figure legend.

claim: Addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the AMT1;3-mcpGFP fusion did not lead to detectable changes in fluorescence intensity in initial tests.
source: In initial tests, addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the AMT1;3-mcpGFP fusion did not lead to detectable changes in fluorescence intensity (FI; data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation.

claim: cpGFP-based sensors for calcium and maltose are exquisitely sensitive to modifications in the linker sequences connecting to the respective binding proteins.
source: However, it is known that the cpGFP-based sensors for calcium and maltose are exquisitely sensitive to modifications in the linker sequences connecting to the respective binding proteins
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior work on cpGFP sensors.

claim: Variant 16 carrying LE/FN as linkers, named AmTrac, showed the highest change in fluorescence intensity among tested variants.
source: Variant 16 (in red), carrying LE/FN as linkers, named AmTrac, showed the highest change in fluorescence intensity.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B with experimental data from screening 24 linker variants.

claim: The FI response of AmTrac was proportional to the ammonium concentration added to the yeast cells.
source: Initial experiments showed that the FI response of AmTrac was proportional to the ammonium concentration added to the yeast cells
evidence: This is supported by titration data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: AMT1;3, AmTrac, and AmTrac-LS have similar Km values for ammonium (55 ± 15 μM, 51 ± 24 μM, and 57 ± 19 μM, respectively).
source: The Kms were 55 ± 15 μM, 51 ± 24 μM, and 57 ± 19 μM, respectively.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B with electrophysiology data from Xenopus oocytes.

claim: AmTrac responses were detectable in single cells, were concentration-dependent, and were readily reversible.
source: AmTrac responses were detectable in single cells, were concentration-dependent, and were readily reversible, demonstrating that AmTrac can be used in vivo to quantify ammonium transport activity and to observe kinetics of the chimeric transporter in response to substrate availability (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D with single cell imaging data.

claim: The unique selectivity of AMT1 for ammonium over potassium was retained for FI responses.
source: The unique selectivity of AMT1 for ammonium over potassium was retained for FI responses (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E with substrate specificity data.

claim: NH4NO3 and (NH4)2SO4 elicited the same FI change as NH4Cl.
source: NH4NO3 and (NH4)2SO4 elicited the same FI change as NH4Cl, demonstrating that chloride does not affect the FI response.
evidence: This is experimental data demonstrating anion independence.

claim: Addition of equimolar concentrations of sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, manganese or zinc did not trigger a change in FI.
source: Furthermore, addition of equimolar concentrations of sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, manganese or zinc did not trigger a change in FI (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E with substrate specificity data.

claim: The FI of AmTrac was relatively low, limiting the dynamic range and the signal-to-noise ratio.
source: The FI of AmTrac was relatively low, limiting the dynamic range and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
evidence: This is an observation about the initial sensor's performance.

claim: Most of the brightest AmTrac variants carried a Ser residue instead of a Glu in the position immediately preceding the mcpGFP insertion.
source: Interestingly, the majority of the brightest variants carried a Ser residue instead of a Glu in the position immediately preceding the mcpGFP insertion
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A with screening data of ~350 random variants.

claim: AmTrac-LS showed improved fluorescence intensity and response compared to the original AmTrac.
source: Figure 5B shows fluorescence intensity and fluorescence response of improved variants normalized to AmTrac values
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B with comparative data.

claim: Mutations D202N, G460D, and T464D known to inactivate AMT1 transporters were introduced into AmTrac.
source: To further corroborate the correlation between transport activity and ammonium-induced FI change, mutations (D202N, G460D, T464D) known to inactivate AMT1 transporters were introduced into AmTrac
evidence: This is described as an experimental approach.

claim: AmTrac variants with inactivating mutations D202N, G460D, or T464D did not show fluorescence response to ammonium addition.
source: Only yeast cells expressing AmTrac showed significantly different responses (SNK test: p<0.01).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6C and 6D with fluorescence response data.

claim: AmTrac variants with inactivating mutations were unable to complement growth of Δmep1,2,3 yeast on ammonium as sole nitrogen source.
source: Figure 6B shows growth complementation of the Δmep1,2,3 or wt yeast expressing AmTrac or its inactive variants
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B with growth assay data.

claim: The allosteric trans-activation mechanism used by AMTs for feedback inhibition at elevated ammonium levels involves phosphorylation of a conserved threonine in the C-terminus.
source: The allosteric trans-activation mechanism used by AMTs for feedback inhibition at elevated ammonium levels
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Suppressor mutations that restore transport activity in AmTrac-T464D were identified through a genetic screen.
source: Figure 7A shows growth of yeast transformed with suppressor mutants
evidence: This is described in the text and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Yeast expressing AmTrac-T464D-A141E grew poorly at high concentrations of ammonium, suggesting high capacity transport activity leading to ammonium toxicity.
source: Note that yeast expressing AmTrac-T464D-A141E grew poorly at high concentrations of ammonium, suggesting high capacity transport activity leading to ammonium toxicity.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7A and interpreted in the figure legend.

claim: Residues corresponding to cis-suppressing mutations reside in the internal pore region of the transporter.
source: Note that residues corresponding to cis-suppressing mutations reside in the internal pore region.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7B and 7C with structural models.

claim: There is a correlation between transport efficiency (growth in 2 mM NH4Cl) and fluorescence change after addition of 1 mM NH4Cl of the suppressor mutants.
source: Correlation between transport efficiency (growth in 2 mM NH4Cl) and fluorescence change after addition of 1 mM NH4Cl of the suppressor mutants.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7E with quantitative data.

claim: AmTrac-T464D-A141E (AmTrac-100µ) has a Km of 3.4 ± 0.56 mM for ammonium.
source: The Km was 3.4 ± 0.56 mM.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8A with electrophysiology data.

claim: AmTrac-100µ represents a low affinity sensor variant with approximately 100-fold higher Km than AmTrac.
source: Comparison of Km values between AmTrac (~50 µM) and AmTrac-100µ (3.4 mM) shown in Figures 4B and 8A
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the Km values in Figures 4B and 8A.

claim: mcpGFP was successfully inserted into the central loop of AMT1;2 from Arabidopsis to create AmTrac1;2.
source: To test whether the strategy of creating activity state sensors by mcpFP insertion is generalizable, we inserted mcpGFP into the central loop of other ammonium transporters; that is, the paralog AMT1;2 from Arabidopsis
evidence: This is described in the text and shown in Figure 9.

claim: mcpGFP was successfully inserted into the central loop of MEP2 from yeast to create MepTrac.
source: To test whether the strategy of creating activity state sensors by mcpFP insertion is generalizable, we inserted mcpGFP into the central loop of other ammonium transporters; that is...the distantly related yeast ammonium transceptor MEP2
evidence: This is described in the text and shown in Figure 9.

claim: AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac both showed fluorescence response to ammonium addition.
source: Fluorescence response of Δmep1,2,3 yeast expressing AmTrac1;2, MepTrac or MepTrac-H194E to NH4Cl at the indicated concentrations at pH 4 or 6.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9B with fluorescence response data.

claim: MepTrac-H194E, carrying an inactivating mutation, did not show fluorescence response to ammonium.
source: Figure 9B shows fluorescence response data for MepTrac-H194E
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9B with fluorescence response data.

claim: Genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors are powerful tools for characterizing in vivo processes involved in cell signaling and physiology.
source: Genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors are powerful tools for characterizing in vivo processes involved in cell signaling and physiology.
evidence: This is a general statement about the utility of biosensors.

claim: Fluorescent biosensors offer new tools for genetic screens and for screening chemical libraries to identify new drugs.
source: They offer new tools for genetic screens, for example, for identifying regulatory networks, or they can be used for screening chemical libraries to identify new drugs (Bermejo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bermejo et al., 2013.

claim: FRET sensors for small molecules allow monitoring of steady state levels and dynamic changes of analytes such as ions, signaling compounds, metabolites and substrates of proteases.
source: The existing tools, that is, FRET sensors for small molecules allow us to monitor steady state levels and dynamic changes of analytes such as ions, signaling compounds, metabolites and substrates of proteases (Okumoto et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Okumoto et al., 2012.

claim: Tools for measuring the activity of transporters in vivo have been limited to electrophysiology prior to this work.
source: However, tools for measuring the activity of transporters in vivo have been limited to electrophysiology, which can not differentiate between transporter isoforms, and is difficult to use for measuring transporter activity in cells in live tissues or even subcellular compartments.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of existing methods.

claim: Electrophysiology cannot differentiate between transporter isoforms.
source: However, tools for measuring the activity of transporters in vivo have been limited to electrophysiology, which can not differentiate between transporter isoforms
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of electrophysiology.

claim: A prototype for activity sensors was developed using ammonium transporters conserved from archaebacteria to higher plants and metazoa, including the human Rhesus factors.
source: Here we developed a prototype for such activity sensors using the important class of ammonium transporters conserved from archaebacteria to higher plants and metazoa, including the human Rhesus factors.
evidence: This is the main finding of the manuscript.

claim: The fluorescence-based sensors make use of the effect of conformational rearrangements in AMTs/MEPs transceptors on the fluorescence emitted by circularly permutated mcpGFPs inserted into an intracellular loop.
source: We made use of the effect of conformational rearrangements in AMTs/MEPs transceptors on the fluorescence emitted by circularly permutated mcpGFPs that have been inserted into an intracellular loop of the transporters.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the sensor.

claim: These fluorescence-based sensors report the activity of the transporter in vivo and can be used to quantify the activity of a specific transporter in vivo.
source: These fluorescence-based sensors report the activity of the transporter in vivo and can be used to quantify the activity of a specific transporter in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: Information on the activity of transporters is relevant for determining the regulation of individual isoforms in live cells, to identify and characterize regulators, to monitor transport in cells otherwise inaccessible to transport measurements, and to characterize subcellular transport processes in living tissues.
source: Information on the activity of transporters is relevant for determining the regulation of individual isoforms in live cells, to identify and characterize regulators, to monitor transport in cells otherwise inaccessible to transport measurements, and to characterize subcellular transport processes in living tissues.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential applications of the technology.

claim: In contrast to the interpretation of results from crystallization studies, AMTs and MEPs both change conformation during transport.
source: We show here that, in contrast to the interpretation of results from crystallization studies (Khademi et al., 2004), AMTs and MEPs both change conformation during transport
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the fluorescence data from the sensors.

claim: AMTs and MEPs most probably do not function as 'passive gas channels'.
source: and thus most probably do not function as 'passive gas channels'.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of conformational changes.

claim: The nature of the conformational changes will require crystallization of the transporter in different states to be fully understood.
source: The nature of the conformational changes, which here are monitored in ensembles, will require crystallization of the transporter in different states, as recently achieved for a variety of transporters (Forrest and Rudnick, 2009; Shimamura et al., 2010; Jiang et al., 2012; Krishnamurthy and Gouaux, 2012).
evidence: This is speculation about future work needed, supported by citations to similar work on other transporters.

claim: A circularly-permutated form of GFP was inserted into the center of the cytosolic loop in AMT1;3 (and AMT1;2 and MEP2) at the pseudo-symmetry axis between the two antiparallel repeats of the transporter to create sensors that report substrate binding.
source: To create sensors that report substrate binding, a circularly-permutated form of GFP (Tian et al., 2009) was inserted into the center of the cytosolic loop in AMT1;3 (and AMT1;2 and MEP2) at the pseudo-symmetry axis between the two antiparallel repeats of the transporter.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: The characteristics of the AmTrac fluorescence response strongly indicate that AmTrac sensors measure processes that occur during the transport cycle, or are intimately and quantitatively connected to transport activity.
source: The characteristics of the AmTrac fluorescence response, namely (i) the indistinguishable transport and fluorescence response kinetics, (ii) the reversibility, (iii) the tight link between transport activity for the FI response, (iv) the correlated shifts in affinity for ammonium transport and FI response, and (v) the restoration of the FI response by reconstitution of transport activity in suppressor mutants, strongly indicate that AmTrac sensors measure processes that occur during the transport cycle, or are intimately and quantitatively connected to transport activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: The data do not exclude the possibility that the sensors report extracellular binding of ammonium and therefore measure extracellular ammonium levels rather than activity.
source: Since binding of the substrate to the transporter is part of the transport cycle, our data do not exclude the possibility that the sensors report extracellular binding of ammonium and therefore measure extracellular ammonium levels rather than activity.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of an alternative interpretation of the data.

claim: AMTs have been suggested to function as both transporters and receptors for ammonium.
source: AMTs have been suggested to function as both transporters and receptors for ammonium (Lima et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lima et al., 2010.

claim: Other transporters with a dual function as transporters and signaling proteins include UhpT from E. coli, Pho84p and GAP1p from Saccharomyces, and Chl1 from Arabidopsis.
source: Other transporters with a dual function as transporters and signaling proteins include UhpT from E. coli (Schwöppe et al., 2003), Pho84p and GAP1p from Saccharomyces (Thevelein and Voordeckers, 2009) and Chl1 from Arabidopsis (Ho et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The mechanism by which signaling is transmitted through transceptors is unclear, specifically how substrate binding or conformational rearrangements during the transport cycle are necessary for triggering the receptor activity.
source: The mechanism by which signaling is transmitted is unclear, specifically how substrate binding or conformational rearrangements during the transport cycle are necessary for triggering the receptor activity.
evidence: This is a statement about gaps in current knowledge.

claim: Some transporter-like receptors, such as the glucose transporter-like SNF3p and RGT1p from S. cerevisiae, appear to be unable to transport, suggesting that binding is sufficient for triggering a conformational rearrangement that is detected by intracellular signaling proteins.
source: Some transporter-like receptors, such as the glucose transporter-like SNF3p and RGT1p from S. cerevisiae, appear to be unable to transport, suggesting that binding is sufficient for triggering a conformational rearrangement that is detected by intracellular signaling proteins (Thevelein and Voordeckers, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Thevelein and Voordeckers, 2009.

claim: The yeast Pho84 phosphate transceptor functions both in phosphate transport and mediates activation of the protein kinase A pathway.
source: The yeast Pho84 phosphate transceptor functions both in phosphate transport and mediates activation of the protein kinase A pathway.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Pho84 function.

claim: Phosphate analogs that do not appear to be transported by Pho84 retain signaling activity, consistent with the hypothesis that a complete transport cycle is not required for signaling.
source: The finding that phosphate analogs that do not appear to be transported retain signaling activity is consistent with the hypothesis that a complete transport cycle is not required for signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations from the literature.

claim: Further analyses of Pho84 suggested that ligand binding is insufficient for signaling, therefore the receptor activity is triggered by specific conformational rearrangements that occur during a specific phase of the transport cycle.
source: However, further analyses suggested that ligand binding is insufficient for signaling, therefore the authors concluded the receptor activity is triggered by specific conformational rearrangements that occur during a specific phase of the transport cycle (Popova et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Popova et al., 2010.

claim: Mutations in the presumed proton-binding site of Pho84 severely reduced transport but not signaling, demonstrating that transport and signaling activities are separable.
source: Mutations in the presumed proton-binding site severely reduced transport but not signaling, demonstrating that transport and signaling activities are separable (Samyn et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Samyn et al., 2012.

claim: Combined analysis of the action of amino acid analogs and mutagenesis of the putative binding site of GAP1 indicated that signaling requires a ligand-induced conformational change that corresponds to a step in the transport cycle but does not appear to require the full cycle.
source: Combined analysis of the action of amino acid analogs and mutagenesis of the putative binding site of the amino acid transceptor GAP1 on transport and signaling have indicated that, similar as in PHO84, signaling requires a ligand-induced conformational change that corresponds to a step in the transport cycle but does not appear to require a the full cycle (Van Zeebroeck et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Van Zeebroeck et al., 2009.

claim: It is conceivable that the fluorescent change observed in the fluorescent ammonium sensors is due to either (i) ammonium binding, (ii) a specific set of steps in the transport cycle, or (iii) the full transport cycle of the transporter.
source: It is therefore conceivable that the fluorescent change observed in the fluorescent ammonium sensors presented here is due to either (i) ammonium binding, (ii) a specific set of steps in the transport cycle, or (iii) the full transport cycle of the transporter.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism based on knowledge from other transceptors.

claim: Crystal structures of AMTs from E. coli and A. fulgidus did not reveal obvious conformational differences when generated in the presence or absence of ammonium.
source: Crystal structures of AMTs from Escherichia coli (Khademi et al., 2004; Zheng et al., 2004) and Archaeoglobus fulgidus (Andrade et al., 2005) did not reveal obvious conformational differences when generated in the presence or absence of ammonium
evidence: This is supported by citations to crystallography studies.

claim: Observations from crystal structures led to the proposition that AMTs are rigid gas channels.
source: observations that led to the proposition that AMTs are rigid gas channels (Khademi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Khademi et al., 2004.

claim: Electrophysiological studies challenged the hypothesis that AMTs transport the uncharged form ammonia by demonstrating that plant AMTs are electrogenic and show minimal or no ammonia conductivity.
source: Electrophysiological studies challenged the hypothesis that AMTs transport the uncharged form ammonia by demonstrating that plant AMTs are electrogenic and show minimal or no ammonia conductivity (Mayer et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mayer et al., 2006.

claim: The transport of the charged form of ammonium is supported by the finding that mutations in the pore release the transporter from a gating control, leading to massively increased transport capacity and an up to 100-fold increase in the Km.
source: The transport of the charged form of ammonium is further supported by the finding that mutations in the pore release the transporter from a gating control, leading to massively increased transport capacity and an up to 100-fold increase in the Km (Figure 8A; Loqué et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 8A and citation to Loqué et al., 2009.

claim: Evidence was provided for the existence of open and closed states by demonstrating an allosteric feedback inhibition of transport activity by phosphorylation of residues in the trans-activating cytosolic C-terminus.
source: Moreover, we provided evidence for the existence of open and closed states by demonstrating an allosteric feedback inhibition of transport activity by phosphorylation of residues in the trans-activating cytosolic C-terminus (Loqué et al., 2007; Lanquar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Loqué et al., 2007 and Lanquar et al., 2009.

claim: The fluorescence response of AmTrac variants and MepTrac supports the hypothesis that AMT1;3, AMT1;2 and MEP2 undergo conformational changes during transport.
source: The fluorescence response of AmTrac variants and MepTrac supports the hypothesis that AMT1;3, AMT1;2 and MEP2 undergo conformational changes during transport.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from the sensors.

claim: The results are consistent with the hypothesis that TMH-V and -VI of AMT move relative to each other as a result of ammonium binding or during ammonium translocation, thus affecting the conformation of L5–6 and thereby gating the inserted mcpGFP.
source: Our results are consistent with the hypothesis that TMH-V and -VI of AMT move relative to each other as a result of ammonium binding or during ammonium translocation, thus affecting the conformation of L5–6 and thereby gating the inserted mcpGFP.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and structural knowledge.

claim: cpGFP has successfully been deployed to monitor conformational changes in a variety of proteins including calmodulin, metal ion binding domains, a periplasmic sugar binding protein, PKG isoforms for measuring cGMP, and a voltage sensing domain of a protein phosphatase.
source: cpGFP has successfully been deployed to monitor conformational changes in a variety of proteins, for example, calmodulin (Baird et al., 1999; Nagai et al., 2001, 2004; Nakai et al., 2001), metal ion binding domains (Baird et al., 1999; Mizuno et al., 2007), a periplasmic sugar binding protein (Marvin et al., 2011), PKG isoforms for measuring cGMP (Nausch et al., 2008), and a voltage sensing domain of a protein phosphatase (Ci-VSP) (Gautam et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: None of the existing cpGFP sensors measures activity; they report ensemble changes in conformational states of the respective proteins.
source: While none of the sensors measures activity, they report ensemble changes in conformational states of the respective proteins.
evidence: This is a statement distinguishing the current work from prior cpGFP sensors.

claim: Insertion of cpGFP can be more widely used to monitor activity states of proteins, specifically ammonium transporters.
source: Here we demonstrate that insertion of cpGFP can be more widely used to monitor activity states of proteins, specifically ammonium transporters.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the successful creation of multiple sensors.

claim: The pseudo-symmetry of AMTs with an inverted repeat of a five TMH containing domain is comparable to that found in the LeuT transporter.
source: Interestingly, the pseudo-symmetry of AMTs with an inverted repeat of a five TMH containing domain is comparable to that found in the LeuT transporter (Krishnamurthy and Gouaux, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Krishnamurthy and Gouaux, 2012.

claim: LeuT carries a substrate-binding site at the interface of the two repeats and undergoes a transport cycle for which multiple states have been identified.
source: LeuT carries a substrate-binding site at the interface of the two repeats and undergoes a transport cycle for which multiple states have been identified (Forrest and Rudnick, 2009; Rudnick, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Forrest and Rudnick, 2009 and Rudnick, 2011.

claim: The transport pore of the AMTs is located between the two pseudo-symmetric halves, with TMH-V and -VI carrying key residues for ammonium translocation.
source: Similarly, the transport pore of the AMTs is located between the two pseudo-symmetric halves, with TMH-V and -VI (connected by L5–6) carrying key residues for ammonium translocation.
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge and prior studies.

claim: The data are consistent with the occurrence of structural rearrangements during transport; crystal structures for different states will be required to determine the conformational state during transport.
source: Our data are consistent with the occurrence of structural rearrangements during transport; crystal structures for different states will be required to determine the conformational state during transport.
evidence: This is a conclusion and statement about future work needed.

claim: An in vivo reporter of activity states for a set of ammonium transporters was developed.
source: In summary, we developed an in vivo reporter of activity states for a set of ammonium transporters.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript.

claim: The combination of two ammonium transport activity sensors from different organisms will be useful for dissecting endogenous control mechanisms.
source: The combination of two ammonium transport activity sensors from different organisms will be useful for dissecting endogenous control mechanisms, because heterologous proteins are not expected to be subject to the same regulatory control and can thus serve as references.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of the sensors.

claim: AmTrac and MepTrac will be deployed in both Arabidopsis roots and in yeast to study their regulation in vivo and to identify regulators.
source: As a next step, we will deploy AmTrac and MepTrac in both Arabidopsis roots and in yeast to study their regulation in vivo and to identify regulators.
evidence: This is a statement about planned future work.

claim: The measurement of flux through a transporter by reporting state changes might be applicable to other transporters or enzymes for monitoring in vivo fluxes.
source: The measurement of flux through a transporter by reporting state changes, as shown here, might be applicable to other transporters or enzymes for monitoring in vivo fluxes, for example, in the context of neurotransmission.
evidence: This is speculation about the broader applicability of the approach.

claim: Such in vivo flux analyses will aid in understanding the mode of action of proteins and may serve as tools for drug discovery.
source: Such in vivo flux analyses will aid in understanding the mode of action of proteins and may serve as tools for drug discovery.
evidence: This is speculation about potential applications.
